title: Best Wi-Fi Security & Public Wi-Fi Tools Compared
metaDescription: Compare VPNs and a travel router for public Wi-Fi security, scored on one published rubric.
intro: Public Wi-Fi networks expose you to serious risks like data theft and malicious attacks. Whether you're working from a café, connecting at hotels, or using campus networks, the right security tools can protect your privacy and sensitive information from cybercriminals.

verdict.summary: NordVPN and Surfshark VPN tie for the top score on these five criteria; NordVPN is listed first only because ties are ordered alphabetically. Both connect automatically on public Wi-Fi, encrypt all your traffic and block malicious sites; Surfshark VPN covers unlimited devices, and NordVPN up to 10 at once. A GL.iNet travel router protects every device that joins it, including ones that can't run a VPN app, but it takes more setup and its encryption depends on the VPN service you run on it. Speed isn't scored, because we haven't measured it. The EFF has retired its HTTPS Everywhere extension; use your browser's built-in HTTPS-only mode instead.

faqs.question: Is public Wi-Fi really that dangerous?
faqs.answer: Yes, public Wi-Fi poses serious risks including data theft, man-in-the-middle attacks, and malware distribution. Cybercriminals often target coffee shops, hotels, and airports because users frequently access sensitive information on these networks.

faqs.question: Do I need a VPN if I only browse regular websites?
faqs.answer: Most sites now use HTTPS, which already encrypts what you send to them, but on public Wi-Fi the network operator can still see which sites you visit, and a fake hotspot can try to intercept connections. A VPN encrypts all your traffic and hides your IP address from the sites you visit, though they can still identify you through cookies and logins.

faqs.question: Can I use free VPNs for public Wi-Fi security?
faqs.answer: Free VPNs often have severe limitations like data caps, slow speeds, and questionable privacy practices. Some even log and sell user data. For reliable public Wi-Fi protection, invest in a reputable paid VPN service.

faqs.question: How can I tell if a Wi-Fi network is secure?
faqs.answer: Look for networks that require passwords (WPA2/WPA3 encryption) and verify the official network name with staff. Avoid open networks or those with suspicious names. Even on password-protected networks, use additional security tools like VPNs.

faqs.question: What should I do if I accidentally used unsecured Wi-Fi?
faqs.answer: Immediately disconnect from the network and change passwords for any accounts you accessed. Run antivirus scans on your devices, monitor your accounts for suspicious activity, and consider enabling two-factor authentication for added security.
